ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Max and Moritz have drawn a square $5 \times 5$ and marked the centres of the small squares. Afterwards, they draw obstacles and then find out in how many ways it is possible to go from $A$ to $B$ using the shortest way avoiding the obstacles and going from centre to centre only vertically and horizontally. How many shortest paths are there from $A$ to $B$ under these conditions?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a 5×5 grid, and there is a black dot at the center of each small square. The arrow of A points to the upper-left corner center point, and the arrow of B points to the lower-right corner center point. Record the center points by row and column as (r,c), then A=(1,1), B=(5,5). The thick black obstacles in the figure block movement between these adjacent center points: (2,2)-(3,2), (2,3)-(3,3), (2,4)-(2,5), (3,3)-(3,4), (3,4)-(4,4), (4,1)-(4,2), (4,2)-(5,2). Reasoning: The shortest path from A to B needs 4 steps to the right and 4 steps downward, so only consider going right and downward. Let f(r,c) be the number of shortest paths reaching (r,c), f(1,1)=1; each point is contributed by the point above and the point on the left, but if there is an obstacle in between, that contribution is not counted. Filling the table row by row gives: row 1 [1,1,1,1,1]; row 2 [1,2,3,4,1]; row 3 [1,1,1,4,5]; row 4 [1,1,2,2,7]; row 5 [1,1,3,5,12]. Therefore the number of shortest paths to B=(5,5) is 12.

Afterwards, they draw obstacles and then find out in how many ways it is possible to go from $A$ to $B$ using the shortest way avoiding the obstacles and going from centre to centre only vertically and horizontally. How many shortest paths are there from $A$ to $B$ under these conditions?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Max and Moritz have drawn a square $5 \times 5$ and marked the centres of the small squares. Afterwards, they draw obstacles and then find out in how many ways it is possible to go from $A$ to $B$ using the shortest way avoiding the obstacles and going from centre to centre only vertically and horizontally. How many shortest paths are there from $A$ to $B$ under these conditions?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a 5×5 grid, and there is a black dot at the center of each small square. The arrow of A points to the upper-left corner center point, and the arrow of B points to the lower-right corner center point. Record the center points by row and column as (r,c), then A=(1,1), B=(5,5). The thick black obstacles in the figure block movement between these adjacent center points: (2,2)-(3,2), (2,3)-(3,3), (2,4)-(2,5), (3,3)-(3,4), (3,4)-(4,4), (4,1)-(4,2), (4,2)-(5,2). Reasoning: The shortest path from A to B needs 4 steps to the right and 4 steps downward, so only consider going right and downward. Let f(r,c) be the number of shortest paths reaching (r,c), f(1,1)=1; each point is contributed by the point above and the point on the left, but if there is an obstacle in between, that contribution is not counted. Filling the table row by row gives: row 1 [1,1,1,1,1]; row 2 [1,2,3,4,1]; row 3 [1,1,1,4,5]; row 4 [1,1,2,2,7]; row 5 [1,1,3,5,12]. Therefore the number of shortest paths to B=(5,5) is 12.
